openings.claim: Routing a recoverability tether through a guide eye could keep the plate seated against guide contacts during strokes; this is unmeasured coupling.
openings.delta: A is a strip guide bolted through existing carriage slots, contacting only unmarked plate regions. B is a detachable wire tether with a removable loop around the unmarked plate end. Intact A×B routes B through a low eye drilled in A, redirecting tension toward guide contacts. Link-broken bypasses that eye while retaining every guide part and the same tether, endpoints and separation limit.
openings.prediction: Baseline: supplied unretained drift is 6 mm after five strokes; twenty-stroke drift is unknown. A alone constrains contact directions but may permit lift or escape. B alone limits separation but may permit drift. Intact predicts less lift/drift than bypass at matched initial tether tension. Nearest rival is additive guide restraint plus tether restraint: it predicts no routing-specific improvement. If both pass equally, or routing only increases tension, coupling is unsupported.
openings.probe: First check clearance and detachable-loop access without touching the marked edge. Use only intact and bypass as the two retention configurations; baseline/A-alone/B-alone are explicit untested controls because the configuration cap forbids their additional fabrication trials. For each configuration, run three twenty-stroke trials, ending with the weaker-magnet spare, and three timed removal/return checks wearing gloves. Measure displacement against starting marks, tether pull with the scale, seating/lift and time. Keep contacts, tether length, initial tension and stroke procedure matched; bypass only the interface. A routing-specific seating change supports an interface effect, but without isolated-parent trials does not establish superadditivity. Record setup minutes and any loop retensioning or guide adjustment; stay within eighty fabrication and twenty observation minutes.
assumptions: Slot geometry permits a strip guide and low routing eye outside stroke clearance; this indispensable clearance is unprovided.
Wire can hold a removable, glove-operable loop without slipping, damaging either existing part or contacting the working edge.
Defeat: bypass tension cannot be matched, wire capacity is insufficient, guide contact distorts, drift exceeds 1 mm, or removal/return exceeds sixty seconds.
Abandon this probe if layout requires modifying plate/carriage, obstructing the exposed 30 mm edge, entering clearance or detaching rails.

assessment: One conditional physical hypothesis merits a clearance-first probe. Geometry, wire capacity and glove operation remain unknown; no deployment or reliable retention claim.
